task_name: The press of gate 1, refused to anything that is not the page

rubric.result: The objective promises four things and the diff produces all four. (a) 'POST /spec-freeze freezes': SpecFreezeRoute.freezing asks freeze.execute(new FreezeSpecParams({root, repository})) with the root and repository read off held().conversation, so the page sends no parameters. (b) 'answers the date and the pull request': the FROZEN branch sends 200 {status: SpecFreezeState.FROZEN, on: frozen.on, pullRequest: frozen.pullRequest}. (c) 'refuses with an explicit code': 403 gate-not-from-the-page, 400 no-coordinating-session, and SpecFreezeRefusal projecting NO_SPEC/ALREADY_FROZEN/NOT_FREEZABLE onto no-epic-spec/spec-already-frozen/spec-not-freezable, plus PlanFailure to PlanCollapse. (d) 'a caller with no key first of all - without asking the freeze': `if (!key.holds(request.get(GateKey.HEADER)))` is the first statement of the handler, before held.held() and before any call on the use case, and the two tests that hit it assert `freeze.asked` is empty over a double whose answer throws 'the freeze must not be asked'. Nothing the objective names is missing.

The TDD line asks for `it('a post with no gate key is refused as gate-not-from-the-page and the freeze is never asked')` with '403, the literal body, and the FreezeSpec double untouched'. The test at spec-freeze-route.test.ts:345 carries that name verbatim and asserts exactly those three: `expect(response.status).toBe(403)`, `expect(await response.json()).toEqual({code: 'gate-not-from-the-page', detail: 'gate 1 answers only a request carrying the key the page was given'})` (a whole-body toEqual, not a substring), and `expect(freeze.asked).toEqual([])`. The input is the same one the plan names: a POST carrying no x-gate-key against a real listening server. Its declared boundary pair is there too (line 362): the key is taken out of a GET made with `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>` and posted back, answering 200 with the date and the pull request - the plan's 'the key a GET handed to a request whose Origin was the server's own'. The other three names in **Tests:** appear literally as well.

The one Contract block is for backend/src/infrastructure/spec-freeze-route.ts and the diff states it name by name. SpecFreezeOutcome is an Object.freeze with exactly the six members and exactly the six literals of the block (accepted, gate-not-from-the-page, no-coordinating-session, no-epic-spec, spec-already-frozen, spec-not-freezable). `static freezing(held: CoordinatingSessions, freeze: FreezeSpec, key: GateKey): RequestHandler` matches parameter names, order and return type. The prose of the task is honoured too: 403 for the key, 400 for no-coordinating-session, a Projection over FreezeOutcome for the other three, and the pinned detail - `the spec is not freezable: ${findings.length} finding(s) remain, ${where}` with `where` being `the first on line ${first.line}` or `the first is ${first.code}` when the finding has no line, which is character-for-character the plan's sentence. FROZEN answers 200 {"status":"frozen","on":…,"pullRequest":{number,url}} (SpecFreezeState.FROZEN is the literal 'frozen'), a PlanFailure becomes PlanCollapse.of(cause) and anything else rethrows, and the POST is mounted with no JsonBody middleware. refusal-codes.test.ts folds SpecFreezeOutcome into RequestVocabularies.codes() as asked; no code collides, since SharedOnPurposeAcrossRequestVocabularies was left untouched and the uniqueness assertion is green.

Row by row. D-22 is the row this task implements and it is implemented as written: the freeze has no endpoint a session can reach - the key is only ever minted into a GET body when Browsers.isOurOwnPage holds, and a POST without it is refused with an explicit code (gate-not-from-the-page) instead of obeyed, before the use case is touched. D-6: the freeze is an act of the program behind a button, never a line the conversation writes - nothing in the diff hands the act to a session. D-7: the diff never merges and never writes to a pull request; it only relays the {number,url} FreezeSpec returned. D-10: TypeScript throughout backend/. D-11: the route forms no second opinion about freezability - it projects FreezeOutcome as the use case decided it and only formats findings into a sentence. D-13: nothing is stored; the answer is derived from the outcome of the call. D-25: no prompt text and no paths pasted anywhere. D-23 is task 6's mechanism and this diff does not bear on it. No row is reopened.

Exemplars: SpecFreezeRefusal is a line-by-line imitation of CoordinatingSessionRefusal in backend/src/infrastructure/coordinating-session-route.ts (the named exemplar) - the same Projection('refusal', [...]) shape, the same `of` entry point, the same PlanFailure/PlanCollapse catch, and the same 'if the outcome is not the accepted one, refuseAs' split. The test harness follows backend/__tests__/infrastructure/coordinating-session-route.test.ts: a real listening server, a real fetch, the use case doubled by construction. Rules: conventions/architecture.md's 'One controller per endpoint' says 'The route, its request model with the closed vocabulary of outcomes, and the projections that turn each outcome and each failure into an answer travel together in one module', so SpecFreezeRefusal living inside spec-freeze-route.ts is the rule being obeyed, not a new concept hidden in an old file. Layering holds: infrastructure imports application and domain and nothing imports upward; the key and the vocabulary stay at the boundary. backend/conventions/this-repository.md is satisfied: every refusal is {code, detail}, the codes are kebab-case, 'a refusal our own application judged always answers 400' (the four application refusals do) and 'a refusal of the protocol itself keeps the status HTTP already gives it' (403 for the missing key, beside http.ts's own 403 foreign-origin). English everywhere, per CLAUDE.md and conventions/style.md; no prose in the code; every function hangs off a type. conventions/boundaries.md: the projection outwards is exhaustive and returns a value object (Refusal), and Projection.of raises for a member nobody mapped instead of guessing; the code of each answer is declared beside its detail and never derived from a class name. conventions/decisions.md: no rule is written twice - the wire literal 'frozen' is taken from the existing SpecFreezeState.FROZEN rather than re-spelled. conventions/simplicity.md: the unguarded `const [first] = findings` is correct rather than missing a check, because EpicSpec.isFreezable() is `findings().length === 0`, so NOT_FREEZABLE can never carry an empty list and a guard there would be the unreachable check that document forbids. conventions/defects.md, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary - SpecFreezeOutcome is a frozen vocabulary, not loose strings, and the dispatch over FreezeOutcome has no catch-all: FROZEN is split off explicitly and everything else goes through Projection, which throws 'no refusal declared for <member>' for an unmapped member, so a new member fails visibly; (2) raw map as the return value of logic - none: the logic returns a Refusal value object and the only maps are the payloads handed to Answer.send, which is the last step before the wire; (3) two fields that have to agree - none introduced: no flag, no sentinel; the absent line stays `null` in FreezeFinding and the detail branches on `first.line === null` rather than on an empty string, and SpecFrozen's nullable on/pullRequest are task 6's type, untouched here; (4) an error named for where it happens - no error type is added by this diff. Two things declared rather than filed: the exported type SpecFreezeOutcomeValue has no consumer today, which simplicity.md would ordinarily reach, but every route module in this tree exports the same twin and ActivePlansOutcomeValue is unused in exactly the same way, so it is the host's idiom for a modified module; and the English refusal details will be rendered verbatim inside a Spanish cabin by task 12 - that is the plan's own design (it pinned spec-not-freezable's English detail itself) and CLAUDE.md keeps backend diagnostics English, so the implementer's choice of wording for the other three is the consistent one. The skill backend-engineering:backend-best-practices loaded and turned out to be a router for Python Django/FastAPI references that declares project conventions prevail over it: nothing in it bears on this Express/TypeScript diff. One low finding below, on the two projection entries nothing measures.

Every `-` line in the two test files is the same mechanical change: RunningApi.listening/get/other gain the `freeze: FreezeSpec` parameter and their five call sites are updated. Not one assertion, case or test is removed, relaxed or rewritten - the five pre-existing GET tests keep their statuses and their whole-body toEqual comparisons letter for letter, and each only gains `const freeze = FreezeSpecSpy.neverAsked()`, which makes them stricter rather than weaker, since the POST route now mounted beside them may not be reached. refusal-codes.test.ts has two `+` lines and no `-` line touching an assertion.

The behaviour the objective promises lives in production code: SpecFreezeRoute.freezing in backend/src/infrastructure/spec-freeze-route.ts holds the key check, the coordinating-session guard, the call to the use case, the PlanFailure catch and the FROZEN answer, and SpecFreezeRefusal holds the projection and composes the not-freezable sentence. The tests reach it through a real express server on a real socket with a real fetch, and assert the status and the literal body that came back over the wire; the only double is the use case itself, which conventions/testing.md's table prescribes for a controller ('the use case, by construction'). Nothing asserted here would survive reverting the production lines: `SpecFreezeRoute.freezing` would not exist and the typecheck command would fail before the suite ran. The refusal sentence with its count and line number is produced by SpecFreezeRefusal.#notFreezableDetail, not written in the test.

The three touched paths are exactly the three the **Files:** line declares, all three (modify), and the diff writes nothing inside them that no sentence of the task asks for. Production: the vocabulary, its value type, the refusal projection and the freezing handler are each named by the task's prose or its Contract block. Tests: FreezeSpecSpy, Keys.FROM_ANOTHER_RUN, Mother.frozenOutcome/notFreezableOutcome and RunningApi.posting each exist to serve one of the five tests **Tests:** lists; the harness signature churn is the minimum needed to pass the new collaborator. Nothing named in ### Out of scope is touched: no groom.js, no slices.js, no brainstorming skill, no merge and no write to a pull request, no change to start-plan, implement-plan, the events or the dispatcher, and no attempt to create the epic's branch. The wiring into api-server.ts and the vite proxy are task 9's and correctly absent. There is no hunk on the plan file, so there is no amendment to rule on.

Five new tests. Deterministic: the gate key comes from Keys.RANDOM = Buffer.alloc(size, 7), so it is the same hex string on every run; the dates are fixtures ('2026-09-14') and the FreezeSpecSpy's clock is a frozen `() => new Date('2026-09-14T00:00:00Z')` that is never even reached; the servers bind port 0 on 127.0.0.1, so no fixed port and no network beyond loopback; there is no sleep and no randomness without a seed. Isolated: each test builds its own express app and its own doubles, and the afterEach splices and closes every server RunningApi started, so nothing leaks into the next test and none of them depends on the order of the file. Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on the status and the whole JSON body that came back over a real socket from the production handler; the one assertion on a double, `expect(freeze.asked).toEqual([])`, is the one conventions/testing.md explicitly demands ('every controller test of a refused request also asserts that the use case was not asked'), and it is backed by a double that throws if asked. The control-tower-loop:test-driven-development skill loaded; the only thing in it these tests could be measured against beyond the three properties is 'One thing. "and" in name? Split it.', and the two names carrying an 'and' are the plan's own literal test names, one of them the TDD line verbatim, so it stays out of the findings. Nothing above `low` and nothing worth reporting at all.

findings.what: SpecFreezeRefusal declares three entries and only one of them is measured. No test in the diff drives FreezeOutcome.NO_SPEC or FreezeOutcome.ALREADY_FROZEN through the route, so rewriting either code literal or either detail leaves both verification commands green: refusal-codes.test.ts only asserts that the codes are unique and kebab-case, which any other kebab-case string also satisfies. The controller is the layer that owns these two refusals, and the sweep declared in the report names four mutated lines, none of them these. It stays low because the task's **Tests:** list named five tests and the implementer wrote all five - the gap is the plan's, and the repair is one more test rather than one fewer line, since the plan's own Contract block requires both codes.
findings.evidence: conventions/testing.md: "every refusal, collision and cut is measured at the layer that owns it, or not at all" - the unmeasured lines are `[FreezeOutcome.NO_SPEC, () => new Refusal({ status: SpecFreezeRefusal.#STATUS, code: SpecFreezeOutcome.NO_EPIC_SPEC, detail: SpecFreezeRefusal.#NO_EPIC_SPEC_DETAIL })]` and its ALREADY_FROZEN twin.
